subject: On-prem qualification: offline ops & hardware next steps

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-22T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery call — on-prem qualification follow-up

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard
- Preference: Private on-prem deployment (air-gapped) for inference serving across two data centers (primary + DR).
- Key constraints: no outbound telemetry, strict patch windows (quarterly), signed offline upgrade bundles only, KMS integration via customer HSM, and limited VPN/jump-host access for support.
- Workload: ~2M monthly tokens peak, spiky evening traffic; throughput target 600 reqs/min with <150ms p95 generation for assistant style calls.

Open/technical clarifications we need from your infra team
1) Desired hardware tolerance: do you prefer NVIDIA A100 class or can you accept MA-64 (our recommended 8x A30-equivalent per rack) — want to confirm power/space for racks.
2) Upgrade window: typical ops teams allow 4-hour maintenance windows quarterly — please confirm your maximum allowed duration and blackout dates.
3) Outbound restrictions: we requested confirmation whether a physically removed jump host (air-gap transfer) or encrypted USB transfer for bundles is the only allowed path.
4) Backup/DR expectations and whether snapshot export is allowed off-network in emergencies.

Attachments I’m including:
- redwood-onprem-reqs.pdf (high-level requirements + network diagrams)
- MA-64_hardware-BOM.xlsx (recommended BOM for capacity profile we discussed)
- onprem-upgrade-runbook.pdf (draft offline upgrade flow)

Proposed next steps
- Action (Neptune): Sofia / Daniel to confirm hardware preference (A100 vs MA-64) and max maintenance window by EOD Tues 3/24.
- Action (Redwood): Vivek to produce a one-page final BOM and precise offline bundle size estimate by 3/24.
- Schedule: 30-minute follow-up with Daniel (infra lead) to walk through jump-host procedures — propose Thu 3/25 09:30 PT.
- Procurement: if the BOM looks good, we’ll send a draft SOW and pricing (separate thread) and provide a PO template for air-gapped installs.

If this matches your notes, I’ll lock the follow-up and loop procurement so we can get preliminary pricing out.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick answers and follow-ups: 

Answers:
- Hardware: Our infra team prefers to standardize on A100-class where feasible, but budget constraints mean MA-64 equivalent is acceptable if performance testing passes. Please include latency projections for both options in the BOM.
- Maintenance window: We can allow up to a 6-hour window for major upgrades but prefer to keep quarterly patches to 2 hours if possible.
- Outbound telemetry: We cannot have any persistent outbound telemetry. Support is allowed via a hardened jump host inside our DMZ that we can stand up for the project.

Questions:
1) What does your rollback process look like for an offline OS/model bundle? What’s the expected RTO in the worst case?
2) Do you provide signed images/bundles and a verification tool we can use in our build pipeline?
3) If we choose MA-64, can you confirm how many concurrent streams we can support at the 600 reqs/min target?

I’m attaching our internal sysops checklist and SOC-questions stub that our compliance team will fill out. Let me know if you want to bring Vivek into a short call with Daniel tomorrow morning.

— Sofia

Subject: RE: Discovery call — on-prem qualification follow-up (hardware & offline upgrades)

Hi Sofia / Daniel — quick technical clarifications from the SE side based on Jordan’s notes and your responses: 

Hardware & performance- For the 600 reqs/min target with p95 <150ms we recommend the MA-64 configuration as the cost-effective baseline (8 x A30-equivalent GPUs, 1TB system RAM, NVMe local caching). A100-class will reduce p95 by ~20–30% for long-context models; I’ll include explicit latency estimates in the updated BOM.

Offline upgrade flow (summary)- We publish signed offline bundles (SHA256 + vendor signature). Customer verifies signature locally with our verification binary (open-source) that we provide.
- Upgrade is performed via USB transfer or mounted ISO to the control-plane node; the runbook walks through pre-checks, bundle install, KV cache warmup, and smoke tests.
- Rollback: system keeps previous model/artifact snapshot; rollback time is typically 10–20 minutes for model swap, up to 60 minutes for full OS rollback depending on component restarts.

Support options- Primary: remote ops via jump host (SSH with cert-based authentication + recorded session artifacts).
- Secondary: offline triage bundles (logs + minimal reproduce artifacts) and on-site support as an add-on.

Deliverables we’ll provide by 2026-03-24
- Finalized MA-64 BOM with latency/throughput columns (CSV + XLSX)
- Offline bundle size estimate and verification checksum workflow
- One-page operators runbook (runnable checklist)

A couple quick asks for your team to help us size the install:
1) Confirm if encrypted USB transfer is acceptable or only DMZ jump-host (we need the preferred air-gap transfer pattern).
2) Confirm whether product telemetry should be fully disabled by default (we’ll ship with telemetry toggled off and a signed opt-in bundle if required).

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute technical call Thu 3/25 09:30 PT — propose that slot for the infra walkthrough.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
